candidates.exact_span: Placement of sewage sludge shall not contaminate an aquifer. This shall be demonstrated through one of the following: a. Results of a ground-water monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water scientist. b. A certification by a qualified ground-water scientist may be used to demonstrate that sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether ground-water monitoring is required versus satisfied by certification affects which monitoring obligations apply (B) and how absence of ground-water monitoring data should be classified when only one demonstration pathway is chosen (C).

candidates.exact_span: When a cover is placed on an active surface disposal site, the concentration of methane gas in air in any structure within the surface disposal site shall not exceed 25% of the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active. The concentration of methane gas in air at the property line of the surface disposal site shall not exceed the lower explosive limit for methane gas during the period that the sewage sludge unit is active. Monitoring shall be continuous.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of the 25%-LEL and property-line LEL thresholds change numeric limit applicability and exceedance determinations (A), and the continuous monitoring requirement plus the cover/site-active conditions change whether methane monitoring was required for a given period (B).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods. Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the once-per-permit-life timing, the one-year window from permit effective date, and the 'after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site' sampling point affects whether TCLP monitoring was required in FY2025 (B) and whether missing TCLP results represent a required-but-unreported case versus a non-applicable period (C).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is classified as hazardous waste under Part 261 shifts the operative compliance framework from permit numeric limits to RCRA disposal standards, changing applicable limit comparisons (A) and the monitoring/disposal obligations triggered by a TCLP result (B).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested at the frequency show below in Element 2, Section I.D. for PCBs. Any sludge exceeding a concentration of 50 mg/Kg shall not be surface disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The external frequency reference in Element 2, Section I.D. determines PCB monitoring applicability (B), and the 50 mg/Kg threshold is an enforceable numeric limit whose exceedance changes surface-disposal compliance outcomes (A).

candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is disposed of in a surface disposal site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements unless sewage sludge is placed on an active surface disposal site, and is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the daily-cover exception applies changes which pathogen-control requirements were operative (B) and how missing pathogen-compliance evidence should be interpreted when Class A/B treatment may not have been required (C).

candidates.exact_span: When reporting on the DMR, list pathogen reduction level attained as A, B, or C (daily cover). When reporting how compliance was met, list Alternative 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 for Class A, or Alternative Number 1, 2, 3, or 4 for Class B, on DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These DMR reporting fields define expected documentary evidence of pathogen compliance; different interpretation of what must be reported affects monitoring/reporting obligations (B) and classification of missing or incomplete DMR entries (C).

candidates.exact_span: All 6 alternatives require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 1000 MPN/g fecal coliform threshold (and the truncated Salmonella criterion continuing in the segment) is an enforceable numeric limit; different interpretation of the limit basis or applicability to a measured result changes exceedance determinations under Purpose A.
